destination.note: What you paste is hidden once saved; only the host shows. Automations in the same project share it.
destination.viaCoordinator: You can also give it to the coordinator in a conversation (it stays in the history).

discard.body: The new version ({{digest}}) is discarded and the one running stays. It cannot be brought back from the screen (the coordinator can, if asked).
discard.title: Discard the new version?

hook.cli: On this PC, the CLI sends it too ({{command}}).
hook.example: Example call (the URL read from a secret value)
hook.keyNote: <KEY> is a number for each occurrence (a version, say). Sent again with the same value, it counts once. <FILE> is the JSON to hand over; with nothing to hand over, use --data '{}'.
hook.offer: To call it over HTTP from other tools, <make>make a receiving URL</make>. You can then give other tools a URL (calls reach it only from inside the VPN).
hook.remade: The URL was made anew. A call to the previous URL gets 404. Replace the value the caller uses.
hook.remakeBody: A new URL is made and the current one stops working at once. Use it when the URL leaked or the caller changes.
hook.remakeCaller: Until the caller takes the new value, “{{name}}” won’t run from HTTP.
hook.remakeCallerAt: It was last called over HTTP at {{time}}. Until the caller takes the new value, “{{name}}” won’t run from HTTP.
hook.secret: Anyone who knows the URL can set it off. Don’t paste it into conversations or repos; keep it in the caller’s secret values. Calls reach it only from this PC’s network (inside the VPN): they don’t arrive from outside services such as GitHub.
